meta_title: Not a Pepper Alternative: Keep Pepper, Add Voice Ordering
meta_desc: Add spoken ordering beside Pepper, with no second rollout. Accounts say each order into an app and check it first. A Pepper alternative that runs beside it.

hero.h1: Not A Pepper Alternative: Keep Pepper, Add Voice
hero.lead: Get orders off the phone without a second rollout. VoiceOrder Solutions sits beside Pepper: accounts speak to our app, review each line, then send. Their orders land timestamped and ready for your desk, and most distributors have it running in 24 to 48 hours.

problem.h2: Why an alternative to Pepper gets searched for
problem.lead: Pepper, made by Pomegranate Technologies, sells an AI platform to independent distributors. It includes an online storefront, an AI tool called Order Agent that enters orders, and tools for sales, finance, pricing and marketing. It is a lot of product, and most of it earns its place. What sends a buyer to look at a Pepper competitor is usually one small problem, not the whole platform.

cards.h3: The phone accounts are still phoning
cards.body: A storefront only helps the kitchens that open it. The rest keep calling, texting and leaving voicemails at the end of a shift, and those are the orders your desk still writes up by hand.

cards.h3: Your team checks what Order Agent read
cards.body: Order Agent takes the voicemail, text, photo or PDF the kitchen already sent and turns it into an order. Pepper's own product page shows no step where the kitchen checks what was read. So your order desk is the first to see the order written down.

cards.h3: One more rollout is the last thing you need
cards.body: Pepper publishes 35 to 90 days for a typical go-live, across five phases, with a setup manager and an engineer assigned to you. That is fair for a platform that size. Going through something like it again just to fix phone orders is not, and no Pepper alternative should ask you to.

features.h2: A Pepper alternative that adds instead of replacing

rows.h3: They talk. It comes out as a list.
rows.body: A chef counts the walk-in and says what is short. Each item turns into a line you can read, with the quantity beside it. Nothing to type, no time on hold, and no voicemail for your team to piece together in the morning.
bullets: They press to speak, then read the lines back before sending
From the cooler or the line, whatever time the shift ends
Runs on their own iOS or Android phone, with no device from you
Saves 20 to 30 minutes compared with the same order by phone
Nobody writes up a reorder from an account on the app, so the reps get that time to sell

rows.h3: Each account gets a list of its own
rows.body: You hand over the guides each kitchen already buys from. We load each guide with your SKUs and the prices you set for that account, so each item a customer says matches the right SKU.
bullets: Each account sees only what it actually orders from you
Your prices, your SKUs, under your control, not the customer's
Change a guide once and it holds from then on
You keep the catalog; the customer gets the convenience

rows.h3: The order shows up in a shape you already handle
rows.body: Nobody in your office has to work somewhere new. Finished orders go out as email with a PDF, Excel or Word file, or straight into your ERP over the API, over EDI, or into QuickBooks.
bullets: Email goes to a rep or straight to your purchasing team
Over EDI, the API or QuickBooks, nobody on your team retypes it
Your pick, invoice and delivery steps stay exactly as they are
You do not have to remove any software first

rows.h3: Watch stock move as the orders land
rows.body: VoiceOrder Solutions gives you real-time inventory visibility tied to what is being ordered, and the catalog updates as levels change. It does not replace your stock system: that stays in charge, and a demo shows how the levels connect.
bullets: Visibility across the catalog, not just the fast movers
Stockouts surprise you less often when a big order lands late
Stock numbers come from the system you count with today

cards.h2: What Pepper keeps and what the voice step adds
cards.lead: VoiceOrder Solutions is no Pepper replacement, and it is not trying to be one. Adding it means taking nothing out, so the platform you rolled out stays exactly where it is.

items.h3: Keep the storefront, add the voice
items.body: Some accounts are never going to browse a catalog. They will talk instead, late in the evening, from the walk-in. The storefront stays for the ones who tap, and our app picks up the ones who talk.

items.h3: Try it on the accounts still calling
items.body: It goes in beside Pepper with no big setup project. Start with the few accounts that never took to the storefront, and judge it on those before deciding anything bigger.

items.h3: Orders still land in your usual place
items.body: Both feed the system you have, so our app does not change where an order ends up. It arrives by EDI, through the API or in QuickBooks, into the system your people already use, or by email as a file.

midcta.h3: Follow one spoken order from a kitchen to your desk
midcta.body: Book 20 minutes. We take one order through to the format it arrives in, so you can see where it lands beside your Pepper orders.

faq.h2: Questions from distributors who are keeping Pepper

items.q: Do we need a Pepper alternative so kitchens can check their own spoken orders?
items.a: No. Pepper can stay as it is, Order Agent included, while we add an app where kitchens say what they need and check every item themselves. The ones already ordering on Pepper's storefront carry on there. Nothing has to be switched off to try it.

items.q: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Pepper?
items.a: No, not at running the whole business on one platform: storefront, reps, collections and pricing. Pepper is built wide for that, and we are not trying to be. We help with one narrower job: a reorder your account speaks and signs off. Plenty of people looking for a Pepper alternative turn out to want exactly that.

items.q: Is there a link between VoiceOrder Solutions and Pepper?
items.a: None. We have no connection to Pepper and no shared support arrangement. Each product hands its orders to your own system separately, ours by email with a file attached, over EDI or the API, or into QuickBooks. When ours are fed directly into your system, both products' orders end up in the same place. Emailed, ours arrive as a file your team opens like any other.

items.q: Will our accounts be juggling Pepper's storefront and your app?
items.a: They should not have to. Kitchens already ordering through the storefront can stay on it. Offer our app to the ones who still call, text or leave a voicemail, because those orders cost your desk the most time. Customers who keep calling are handled the way they are today. Their calls get no order number from us, because numbers are only given to app orders.

items.q: How quickly can we actually be taking orders?
items.a: Most distributors reach that point in a day or two, and most of their customers send a first order the same day. There is no IT project, and Pepper carries on as normal. That is a much smaller job than the setup window Pepper publishes for its whole platform.

We quote by distributor, so tell us about your operation and we will price it. Pepper quotes too and publishes no rate card. Since you would be keeping Pepper, the figure worth asking for is what our app adds on top.

items.q: Do our customers need new hardware or a tablet?
items.a: No. Our app runs on the phone already in their pocket. We send nothing out, there is nothing to bolt to a counter, and no device for you to support.

items.q: Where do the Pepper details on this page come from?
items.a: Pepper's own website. The module list, the storefront and Order Agent descriptions and the implementation window were all read off usepepper.com on 10 October 2026, including their own post on how long an implementation takes. We have not repeated their marketing numbers here. If any of it has changed since, this page is the thing that is out of date, not them.
